newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA unit SilkAir could break even this yr.
newsitem.headline: SIA unit SilkAir could break even this yr.

text.p: Regional airline SilkAir, a Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) subsidiary, could break even in the current financial year, SIA deputy chairman and chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong said on Wednesday.
Cheong told Reuters in an interview that SilkAir had trimmed its losses to Singapore $3 million for the six months ended September 30, 1996.
"There is a chance that it might break even (for the whole year) and wipe out the S$3 million loss in the second half," Cheong said.
SilkAir made a loss for the last full financial year of S$6 million.
Cheong said there was a possiblity of floating SilkAir in the future but SIA would still seek to have control of the regional airline.
The growth rates for SilkAir were also higher than for SIA because it was growing from a much smaller base, Cheong said.
SilkAir's average growth rate (in capacity terms) since 1990 had been 37 percent a year, he said.
He said SilkAir's role was to develop secondary destinations in Southeast Asia and put them on the global tourist market.
"The airline is still making losses because it is a pioneer in many of these destinations," he said.
